payload.title: Reporting agents inspect predictions and steer publication classifiers
payload.description:
## Intent and boundary

As a Papyrus reporting agent, I want to inspect a Reference's publication-scoped Cyclotron predictions and explicitly submit approve/reject feedback, so that reporting both uses and steers the publication's classifiers with an auditable account of what happened.

Milestone: a usable reporting-and-steering CLI/API contract shared with the existing curation UI, for embedded and remote lab bindings. Design + issue filing authorized here; coding belongs to Claude. Do not redesign Cyclotron, add billing/deployment work, publish articles, or introduce long-lived credentials. Agent ability to steer is required; the governance of agent labels remains an explicit decision below.

Parent PPY-ad3da5 (one content item, one lifecycle): reporting decisions and reasoning stay anchored to the existing story lineage. Coordinate with PPY-b0396f (existing relevance pipeline), PPY-202505 (operator CLI), and PPY-7a0ac8 (shared publication/lab review). This extends their existing primitives for agent usability; it does not replace those epics or repeat their engine/UI implementation.

## Observed current behavior — source at 2f8954068d624f2fb2a0b157a71f975ad90f6850

- `papyrus references list-predictions --config PATH --corpus-key KEY --status current --limit N` exists, but references_commands.py:120 and reference_labels.py:254 select `classified_as` category predictions. Its printed columns omit confidence, classifier/model identity and the relevance label; it is not the relevance approve/reject reader.
- Relevance predictions already exist as current `SemanticRelation` rows with predicate `relevance_decision_is`. relevance_decisions.py:68-109 records Reference lineage/version, label, confidence, probabilities, classifierId `<cyclotron>/<classifier>`, modelVersion, decisionId, fingerprint, timestamp and review selection metadata. `listSemanticRelationsBySubjectState(subjectStateKey: "reference#LINEAGE#current")` is the existing read index (graphql_authoring.py:443); filter predicate/state and match the pinned Reference revision. This is a low-level available API, not an ergonomic reporting command. Do not call confidence calibrated without separate evidence.
- `lib/relevance-decisions.ts:57-81` already builds a UI decision view with confidence, version, label, classes, cyclotron identity and review recommendation. `curationForRelevanceReview` maps an explicit positive label to curation accept; negative labels to reject with reason. UI supports optional explanations; reuse these semantics and transport rather than inventing a second label store.
- `papyrus references review-curation --reference RECORD_ID --action accept --actor ChatGPT --note "reason"` and `... --action reject --reason-code out_of_scope --actor ChatGPT --note "reason"` are supported. references_commands.py:94 delegates to reference_actions.py:169. The latter updates curation status, appends a `reference_curation` Message and a comment relation in separate writes. It preserves authorLabel/note, but this CLI path has no actor-kind/model/platform provenance, selected prediction id/version/fingerprint, output binding, retry key or feedback-application receipt parameters. Caller-supplied authorLabel alone is not verified agent-versus-human identity.
- These curation calls can feed steering, but do not synchronously call the engine. relevance_sweep.py:359-386 sends reviews only when a current relevance decision with decisionId and a curation Message exist. It passes explanation=curationStatusReason, reviewer=Message.authorLabel and review_id=Message.id; the engine deduplicates that review identity. Accepted maps to positive/include; rejected for out_of_scope or policy_exclusion maps to negative/exclude; other outcomes have no label (relevance_decisions.py:155 and docs/cyclotron-priming.md:123). Confirm configured labels instead of assuming vocabulary.
- `papyrus references decide-relevance --config PATH --apply --json` runs the sweep (default without --apply is dry run). It also restores/saves the store, handles priming and decides pending References; it is not a feedback-only command. Our PwnEscape curation accepts did not run this sweep, and we have not verified a corresponding decision or applied feedback. Do not claim they trained or improved a classifier.
- `papyrus references export-relevance-recording --config PATH --output FILE.json` reads the engine log/store without model calls, but is a recording export, not a per-Reference receipt/status interface.
- Existing `lib/publication-cyclotron.ts`, publication-cyclotron-panel.tsx and docs/cyclotron-priming.md:448-483 define pinned accountId/publicationId/bindingRevision, explicit-label review, optional explanation, prediction version/fingerprint, stable retry identity and backend acknowledgement. Reuse these contracts across CLI/API and UI. Host verifies auth; browser-supplied actor/account is not authority. Source existence is not proof of deployed support.
- Story notes already support `--reference REFERENCE_LINEAGE --version N`, independently from consulted/cited links. Observed defect: story_commands.py:102 forwards these; story_reporting.py:253-272 builds metadata; graphql_authoring.py:939-943 strips Message.metadata, so readback loses structured anchors. Reuse/fix through its code owner, never bypass with ad hoc writes.

## Proposed operator contract (names below are proposals, not current commands)

1. Discover eligible bindings with publication/account/classifier/output identity, transport and supported labels. Resolve exact Reference record, lineage and revision. Publication configuration owns transport once; an agent chooses an authorized binding rather than wiring endpoints/credentials per task.
2. Read or request a prediction with structured CLI/API output. Return prediction ID, pinned scope/binding revision, Reference revision/content fingerprint, native label plus explicit approve/reject mapping, model/classifier version and timestamp. Return confidence/probabilities only with specified semantics, and rationale only if actually available. Distinguish pending, failed, missing, stale and current; show provenance unavailable explicitly. Prediction requests may incur work and must be distinct from reads.
3. Submit an explicit approve/reject label with optional explanation. Bind it to the chosen classifier/output/publication and the prediction/Reference revision. Verify authenticated actor and authorization server-side; preserve human/agent identity and agent platform/model/run provenance where known. Do not let the client assert a human identity. Accept a blank explanation without inventing one.
4. Return durable receipt and status retrieval distinguishing recorded, queued, applied and failed, including recoverable partial failure after curation changes. Stored feedback is not proof of retraining, classifier consumption or increased accuracy. Idempotency covers retries across the whole operation, not just engine review ingestion.
5. Corrections/retractions preserve earlier feedback and application history. Old Reference revisions/predictions stay inspectable but are marked stale; reject accidental feedback against the wrong scope or revision.
6. Reporting workflow records prediction/feedback receipt, independent judgment and reasoning as Story Messages with Reference/version anchors. Citation-role promotion alone never creates a training label. Any later reporting-skill update is implementation follow-up, not part of this filing.

Possible command family for discussion: `papyrus references prediction show|request`, `papyrus references feedback submit|show|correct|retract`, and `papyrus classifiers bindings list`, with structured `--json` results. Prefer extending existing operator surfaces after CLI/API owner review; do not promise these commands exist.

## Decisions required before implementation acceptance

- How agent labels count: equal standing, review required, separate weighting, or another explicit policy. Preserve provenance under every policy; do not silently train on a model echoing its own prediction. Discuss independent evidence, agent self-review and conflict handling rather than assuming one policy.
- Define canonical vocabulary: curation accept/reject (admission), classifier include/exclude or configured labels (relevance), approve/reject feedback (judgment). Decide the visible mapping and whether training feedback can be recorded independently from changing curation status. Make coupling explicit; do not change existing semantics silently.
- Define confidence meaning, whether explanation/rationale exists, consistency/revision rules, and what evidence establishes applied/consumed. Do not manufacture rationale, calibrated probability, success or accuracy improvement.

## Acceptance scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: Reporting agents inspect and steer scoped classifiers
  Scenario: Inspect one reference prediction
    Given an authorized publication binding and a current Reference revision
    When an agent reads its prediction
    Then the response identifies the scope, revision, prediction, native label and approve/reject mapping
    And available confidence has defined semantics and model version and timestamp are present
    And missing rationale is identified rather than invented

  Scenario: The same reference has independent publication outputs
    Given the same source in two authorized publications with different classifier outputs
    When an agent reviews one output
    Then only that publication and output receive feedback
    And a binding change or revoked grant prevents a stale request from writing

  Scenario: No current successful prediction
    Given a missing, pending, failed or stale prediction
    When an agent inspects it
    Then its actual state and any available failure are returned
    And no prediction or applied-feedback success is fabricated

  Scenario: Feedback without an explanation
    Given an authorized current prediction
    When an agent submits an explicit label with no explanation
    Then the label is recorded with an absent explanation and a durable receipt

  Scenario: Retry does not duplicate feedback
    Given a request whose response was lost
    When the same authorized request identity is retried
    Then the same receipt is recovered without duplicate feedback or engine application

  Scenario: Agent provenance is preserved
    Given feedback submitted by an authenticated reporting agent
    When a human or agent inspects its audit record
    Then the record identifies it as agent feedback with known provenance
    And it is not presented as a human label or verified through a display name alone

  Scenario: Partial application failure is visible
    Given curation status changed but engine feedback application failed
    When the agent retrieves the receipt
    Then recorded curation and failed or queued feedback are reported separately
    And supported recovery preserves history and prevents duplicate application

  Scenario: A revised reference supersedes its prediction
    Given feedback on an earlier Reference revision
    When a new revision is selected
    Then the earlier prediction and feedback remain auditable as historical
    And current status identifies the prediction as stale until valid replacement work completes

  Scenario: Embedded and remote transports share semantics
    Given equivalent authorized embedded and remote publication bindings
    When the same prediction and review workflow is performed
    Then response states, revision checks, authorization, provenance and receipt semantics agree
    And publication configuration supplies the transport

  Scenario: Citation promotion is independent
    Given a source linked consulted on a story
    When reporting promotes the source to cited
    Then no classifier feedback is silently created
    And an explicit feedback operation can be documented separately in an anchored Story Message
```

## Definition of Done

Claude/code owners implement and verify the agreed contract through executable observable scenarios and the normal PR workflow. Demonstrate the complete reporting agent loop through configured publication bindings without hand-wired endpoints; show verified receipt status and truthful failure states. Reuse current curation and publication review infrastructure and preserve editorial lineages. Resolve and document the open agent-label and vocabulary decisions. No engine redesign, paid-model audit, production rollout, billing work or deployment configuration is implied by this epic.
